name: The mattpyle.com webmaster
description: The webmaster of mattpyle.com, Matt Pyle's personal site about agent-led growth and emerging web standards. Three skills: it answers questions about the site (its writing, projects, changelog, scorecard, and agent-readable surfaces); it audits any site you name for agent-readiness, returning the fast tier as a direct Message and the browser-rendered deep tier as a Task you poll to completion; and it hands you to the audit consultant, a Claude-driven agent that audits a site and says what matters, in a conversation held as a multi-turn Task. Replies are written in the voice of the site's retro webmaster. Unauthenticated and public: no accounts, no payments, and no private data. Audits are rate limited, and the auditor obeys the target's robots.txt.

skills.name: Ask about this site
skills.description: Answers questions about mattpyle.com: who Matt Pyle is, what he has written and built, what has shipped recently, and which agent-readable surfaces the site exposes (agents.md, llms.txt, raw-markdown variants, WebMCP tools, this endpoint). Answers cite site URLs and are compiled from the site's own published content at build time, so they never contradict the pages themselves. One turn: the reply is a direct Message, and there is nothing to poll.
examples: What has shipped on this site lately?
What agent-readable surfaces does this site expose?

skills.name: Audit a site for agent-readiness
skills.description: Audits any site you name for what it says about itself to agents: robots.txt and its AI-agent rules, Content Signals, the sitemap, llms.txt and whether its links resolve, agents.md, the well-known MCP and A2A discovery documents, and whether the homepage and a content page really serve markdown when asked for it. It checks behaviour rather than presence. Name a site and an audit verb, e.g. 'audit example.com', and say 'deep' for the browser-rendered tier that adds Lighthouse per-axis scores and axe-core violation counts from up to three of the site's own pages. The fast tier takes seconds and comes back as a direct Message carrying the report as markdown and as JSON. The deep tier takes minutes and comes back as a Task: poll GetTask with the task's id until its state is TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, and the report is the task's artifact, again as markdown and as JSON. The auditor obeys the target's robots.txt and arrives as steward-audit/0.2.0 (+https://www.mattpyle.com/steward), so one audit is one visitor in the target's log. Audits are rate limited per caller and per day, on a budget shared with the MCP endpoint at https://www.mattpyle.com/mcp; deep audits are capped far lower than fast ones because each spends real browser time on a hosted worker. Reading a Task with GetTask is free.
examples: Run an agent-readiness audit of https://example.com
Run a deep audit of example.com, with Lighthouse and axe
Scan example.com and tell me what it says to agents

skills.name: Talk to the audit consultant
skills.description: A conversation with the audit consultant, a Claude-driven agent that audits a site for agent-readiness and tells you what matters and what to fix first. The model decides the path: whether to audit, which tier, and when to ask you a question. Address it by name: send SendMessage with metadata {"skill": "consult-on-a-site"} and no task id. The reply is a Task whose id is the session. Poll GetTask with that id. TASK_STATE_WORKING means the consultant is working. TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED means it waits for you, and metadata.awaiting says for what: "answer" for a question it asked, "approval" for a deep audit it wants to run (reply "yes" or "no"), or "message" when it has answered and waits for your next message. The status message carries its question or its answer. Reply with SendMessage and message.taskId set to the session's id. CancelTask closes the session. A session ends as TASK_STATE_COMPLETED when it reaches one of its caps or sits idle for 30 minutes, with metadata.ended naming which. New sessions are rate limited per caller and per day, and each session has its own caps on turns, tokens and deep audits. The consultant audits through this site's public MCP endpoint and sees check results, never the audited site's text.
examples: Can you check my site and tell me what matters?
Audit example.com and tell me what to fix first
Is my llms.txt doing anything for agents?
